Métricas del coste de los fallos: reproc: Metrics for the cost of failure: rework, waste, complaints, returns. Quantifying them turns quality into an economic argument and prioritises improvement.

Insumo que entra en el proceso productiv: An input that enters the production process before being transformed. Its incoming checks, specifications and traceability determine the quality of the final product.

Fase del proceso donde se aplica un cont: A stage in the process where an essential check is applied to prevent, eliminate or reduce a food hazard to acceptable levels. Each CCP requires defined critical limits, continuous monitoring and documented records.
Comunicación formal por un incumplimient: A formal communication regarding a failure in raw materials, packaging or services (quality, quantity, deadlines or documentation). Managing claims traceably protects margins and feeds objective supplier evaluation.
Documento o dato que evidencia el cumpli: A document or piece of data that provides evidence that checks and procedures on the plant floor have been met. Digitising records eliminates paper, speeds up audits and turns data into indicators accessible in real time.

Conjunto de prácticas que garantizan que: A set of practices that ensure food does not cause harm to the consumer. It covers hygiene, control of physical, chemical and biological hazards, traceability and regulatory compliance across the whole chain.

Periodo durante el cual un producto mant: The period during which a product maintains its quality and safety conditions. Determining it relies on stability studies and it governs use-by dates and logistics.

Qué es un KPI de calidad y por qué medir: What a quality KPI is and why you should measure it
Un KPI (Key Performance Indicator) de ca: A quality KPI (Key Performance Indicator) is a quantifiable metric that reflects the performance of processes related to food safety, compliance, and continuous improvement in a food company. It isn't about accumulating data for its own sake, but about selecting the quality indicators that actually guide decision-making.

Los KPIs de calidad alimentaria también: Food quality KPIs also make it easier to communicate with other departments and senior management, since they translate the technical complexity of quality work into figures that are easy to understand and compare. This KPI measures the time elapsed between opening a non-conformity and its effective closure. Long resolution times can point to bottlenecks in assigning responsibilities or implementing corrective actions. Reducing this indicator is key to minimizing the impact of deviations on production and product safety.
Este indicador de calidad relaciona el n: This quality indicator links the number of incidents detected to each batch or product reference. It helps identify whether problems are concentrated in specific raw materials, particular production lines, or certain suppliers. (ISO, s.f.). Un porcentaje de cumplimien: (ISO, n.d.). A high compliance percentage reflects the maturity of the management system; a low one points to priority areas for improvement. This KPI also allows you to compare progress across audit cycles and justify investment in training or resources.

This KPI measures the number of complaints received relative to the volume of product delivered or sold. A high rate can point to failures in final quality control, labeling, the cold chain, or allergen management, among other factors. Antes de marcar un objetivo, analiza el: Before setting a target, analyze the history of the last six to twelve months. Without reference data, any target is arbitrary.
Los objetivos deben ser específicos, med: Targets must be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound. For example: "Reduce the average non-conformity resolution time from 12 to 8 days next quarter" is a SMART target; "improve quality" is not.

Un objetivo que resultaba ambicioso hace: A target that seemed ambitious six months ago may now be outdated after rolling out a new production line or changing supplier. Quarterly or half-yearly reviews keep KPIs aligned with operational reality.

responde a un problema que ya ha ocurrid: responds to a problem that has already occurred. Una acción mal documentada es casi tan i: A poorly documented action is almost as useless as never having opened it. For a corrective or preventive action to be effective, it must follow a complete and traceable cycle.
El punto de partida es siempre la identi: The starting point is always identifying the problem or risk. It must be clearly recorded who detected the situation, when, and in what context. Next, a rigorous root cause analysis is essential. Tools such as the 5 whys, the Ishikawa diagram, or fault tree analysis are useful for not stopping at the surface.
Una vez identificada la causa raíz, se d: Once the root cause has been identified, the measures to implement, the people responsible for carrying them out, and a realistic due date are defined. Without an owner and a date, the action becomes just an intention.
Este es el paso que más se omite y el má: This is the step that gets skipped most often and is the most critical. Once the action has been carried out, it's necessary to check whether it has actually eliminated the cause of the problem. The verification must be documented and signed by someone with the authority to validate it.
Solo cuando la eficacia está demostrada: The action can only be closed once effectiveness has been demonstrated. The closure must be recorded with a date, evidence, and the signature of the quality manager.

Un análisis de causa raíz bien ejecutado: A well-executed root cause analysis produces three outcomes: the immediate correction to contain the problem, the corrective action to eliminate the cause, and the preventive action to stop similar situations from occurring in other processes or areas.

Existen diversas herramientas para lleva: There are various tools for carrying out a root cause analysis. The most widely used in the food industry, for their practicality and ease of communication, are the 5 whys method and the Ishikawa diagram (or cause-and-effect diagram).
consiste en preguntar sucesivamente “¿po: consists of repeatedly asking “why?” after each answer given until reaching the root cause of the problem. Generally, three to five iterations are enough to move past the symptoms and reach a structural cause. For example:

No existía un sistema de alerta que avis: There was no alert system to notify the maintenance owner.
El plan de mantenimiento no contemplaba: The maintenance plan didn't include automatic reminders.
La causa raíz no es el detector sin cali: The root cause isn't the uncalibrated detector, but the lack of a preventive maintenance management system. The corrective action must target that level.
, también conocido como diagrama de espi: , also known as the fishbone diagram, is especially useful when a problem has multiple possible causes or involves several departments. It starts from the effect (the problem) and explores the causes grouped into classic categories such as manpower, machinery, materials, method, environment, and measurement. This overall view makes teamwork easier and keeps the analysis from being skewed by a single department's perspective.
Ambas herramientas son complementarias:: Both tools are complementary: the 5 whys help dig deeper into each branch of the Ishikawa diagram, while the diagram ensures that no category of potential causes is overlooked.

Qué es un sistema de gestión de calidad: What a quality management system (QMS) is and what it brings to a food company
Un sistema de gestión de calidad (SGC) e: A quality management system (QMS) is the set of policies, processes, procedures and records that an organization establishes to ensure its products and services systematically meet legal, regulatory and customer requirements. In the food industry, the QMS goes beyond mere certification: it is the backbone that supports the safety, legality and continuous improvement of the entire operation.
Un SGC bien implantado aporta beneficios: A properly rolled-out QMS delivers concrete, measurable benefits. First, it drastically reduces the risk of food safety incidents, since checks are defined, assigned and verified. Second, it facilitates access to major distribution chains and industrial customers that require certifications such as
del sector. En tercer lugar, convierte l: in the sector. Third, it turns quality into a
, al demostrar de forma objetiva y audit: , by objectively and verifiably demonstrating that your company produces with rigor. Finally, it builds an internal culture geared toward prevention and continuous improvement, which translates into fewer reworks, fewer returns and greater operational efficiency.
las principales normas y estándares de c: the main quality standards and regulations
La base legal de cualquier SGC en alimen: The legal basis for any QMS in the food sector starts within the European framework. As established by the
(Reglamento [CE] 178/2002, 2002), los op: (Regulation [EC] 178/2002, 2002), food business operators are primarily responsible for ensuring that the food they market meets safety requirements. A structured QMS is precisely the tool that makes this demonstrable.

Antes de diseñar nada, es imprescindible: Before designing anything, it is essential to know the starting point. A gap analysis compares the company's current situation with the requirements of the chosen standard or reference, whether that's

2. Definición del alcance y la política: 2. Defining the scope and the quality policy.
En alimentación, el SGC integra necesari: In the food sector, the QMS necessarily incorporates the Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) system. This analysis identifies the biological, chemical and physical risks of each process and defines the checks needed to eliminate them or reduce them to acceptable levels.
Cada proceso clave debe quedar documenta: Each key process must be documented: how it's done, who does it, how often and how it's recorded. This is where many quality managers feel the heaviest bureaucratic burden, especially if they work with paper documents or scattered files.
4. Diseño e implantación de procedimient: 4. Designing and rolling out procedures and instructions.

Una vez implantado, el sistema necesita: Once rolled out, the system needs to be verified periodically. Internal audits make it possible to detect deviations before the external auditor arrives and trigger the continuous improvement cycle.
La dirección debe revisar periódicamente: Management must periodically review the QMS results — incidents, non-conformities, objectives — to make strategic decisions that keep the system alive and effective.

La documentación es el esqueleto visible: Documentation is the visible skeleton of any quality management system in the food industry. Without it, there is no traceability, no possible audit and no certification. But managing it efficiently is one of the biggest day-to-day challenges.
Un SGC completo requiere, como mínimo, l: A complete QMS requires, at a minimum, the following documented elements: the quality policy and objectives, the system manual (where required by the chosen reference), standard operating procedures (SOPs), work instructions, HACCP plans and hygiene control plans, and the records that provide evidence of every check carried out.
En cuanto a los registros, su valor es d: As for records, their value is twofold: on the one hand, they demonstrate to an auditor that checks are actually carried out; on the other, they are a data source for detecting trends, anomalies and opportunities for improvement. The most common records include temperature checks, microbiological and physicochemical analyses, cleaning and disinfection records, raw material receiving checks, and the results of internal and external audits.
Respecto a las auditorías, en un SGC mad: As for audits, a mature QMS involves at least three types: internal audits (carried out by the quality team itself), second-party audits (carried out by customers) and third-party audits (carried out by accredited certification bodies). Preparing for and passing these processes competently requires keeping documentation accessible, up to date and organized at all times.

cuando se fabrican productos con y sin a: when products with and without allergens are manufactured in the same facilities without adequate separation measures.
restos de producto que quedan en superfi: product residues left on surfaces, pipes, pumps or mixers can contaminate the next batch.

Qué debe incluir una ficha técnica de pr: What a food product specification sheet should include
Una buena especificación de producto no: A good product specification is not a filler document. It is the technical reference used by production, quality, purchasing, logistics and customers to make decisions. That's why its content must be complete, accurate and verifiable. These are the sections that cannot be missing:
Nombre comercial, denominación legal, có: Trade name, legal name, internal code, product family and document version. It seems basic, but it's common to find specification sheets without a version code or with names that don't match those in the
Lista de ingredientes en orden decrecien: List of ingredients in descending order, allergen declaration (confirmed presence and possible cross-contamination), nutritional information and, where applicable, authorized nutrition or health claims.
Descripción del aspecto, color, textura,: Description of the expected appearance, color, texture, smell and taste, with acceptable tolerance ranges. This section is key for quality control on receipt and dispatch.
pH, actividad de agua (aw), humedad, con: pH, water activity (aw), moisture, salt content, Brix degrees or other relevant indicators depending on the type of product. Each parameter must state the target value and the minimum and maximum limits.

Tipo de envase, material, formato, grama: Type of packaging, material, format, net weight, batch marking and all mandatory information that must appear on the label.

conocen muy bien los puntos débiles de l: know the weak points of specification sheets very well. These are the most repeated failures:
Una ficha sin número de versión y fecha: A specification sheet without a version number and approval date is uncontrollable. If the supplier or customer is working with an old version and the product has changed, the risk is obvious. Many non-conformities in audits come precisely from outdated versions still in circulation.
Omitir un alérgeno presente en la formul: Omitting an allergen present in the formulation, or failing to correctly indicate the risk of cross-contamination, is one of the errors with the greatest legal and safety impact. The allergen declaration must be reviewed every time an ingredient or supplier changes.
Indicar únicamente el valor objetivo sin: Stating only the target value without specifying acceptance limits makes it impossible to make objective decisions during quality control. Every measurable parameter must have its tolerance range.
Si cambia la formulación o el proveedor: If the formulation or the supplier of an ingredient changes and the specification sheet is not updated, the nutritional information may be inaccurate. This affects both legal labeling and the reliability of the documentation for the customer.
Una ficha técnica sin responsable de apr: A specification sheet with no identified approval owner has no documentary validity. It must state who prepared it, who reviewed it and who approved it, together with the corresponding dates.
La ficha técnica debe ser coherente con: The spec sheet must be consistent with the product record in the ERP, with raw material purchasing specifications, and with quality control records. Inconsistencies between documents create confusion and non-conformities.
No estar alineada con el resto del siste: Not being aligned with the rest of the system.

Set up a clear approval workflow.
Cada vez que se produce un cambio releva: Every time a relevant change occurs — a new ingredient, a supplier change, a process modification — a review of the affected spec sheet should be triggered automatically. This link must be built into the change management procedure.
Vincula las fichas a los cambios de form: Link spec sheets to formulation or supplier changes.

Aunque no haya habido cambios, las ficha: Even if nothing has changed, spec sheets must be reviewed at a minimum frequency — usually annual — to confirm they're still valid. This review must be logged.
